Based on the search results, I can provide you with comprehensive information about food temperature acceptance standards for food safety.

## Food Temperature Acceptance Standards

### The Temperature Danger Zone

The most critical concept in food safety is the **"Temperature Danger Zone"** — the range where bacteria can grow rapidly:

- **USDA/FDA standard**: 40°F to 140°F (4°C to 60°C)
- **Australian standard**: 5°C to 60°C (41°F to 140°F)

Food should **NOT** be accepted or left in this temperature range for extended periods.

---

### Cold Food Acceptance Temperatures

| Food Type | Safe Acceptance Temperature |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| Refrigerated perishable foods (dairy, meats, seafood) | **41°F (5°C) or below** |
| Fresh food | **0°C to 4°C (32°F to 39°F)** |
| Frozen foods | **0°F (-18°C) or below** |
| Pharmaceuticals (if applicable) | **2°C to 8°C (36°F to 46°F)** |

---

### Hot Food Acceptance Temperatures

| Food Type | Safe Acceptance Temperature |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| Hot held foods | **135°F (57°C) or above** |
| Cooked vegetables and fruits | **135°F (57°C) or above** |
| Hot food delivery/transport (HACCP/WHO standard) | **149°F (65°C) or above** |

---

### Safe Minimum Internal Cooking Temperatures (Before Acceptance)

| Food | Minimum Internal Temperature |
|------|------------------------------|
| Poultry (whole, ground, or parts) | **165°F (74°C)** |
| Ground meats (beef, pork, veal, lamb) | **160°F (71°C)** |
| Whole cuts of beef, pork, veal, lamb | **145°F (63°C)** + 3 min rest |
| Fish and seafood | **145°F (63°C)** |
| Egg dishes | **160°F (71°C)** |
| Casseroles, leftovers | **165°F (74°C)** |
| Reheated foods | **165°F (74°C)** |

---

### Key Rules for Food Acceptance

1. **The 2-Hour/4-Hour Rule**: Potentially hazardous foods should not be in the danger zone for:
   - **0-2 hours**: Safe to use
   - **2-4 hours**: Use immediately
   - **Over 4 hours**: **Discard**

2. **When receiving deliveries**:
   - Check temperatures immediately upon arrival
   - Reject any cold foods above 41°F (5°C)
   - Reject any hot foods below 135°F (57°C)
   - Reject frozen foods that show signs of thawing

3. **Documentation**: Record temperatures at regular intervals (every 2-4 hours) for HACCP compliance.

---

### International Variations

| Region | Cold Storage Standard | Danger Zone |
|--------|----------------------|-------------|
| United States (FDA/USDA) | ≤40°F (4.4°C) | 40°F – 140°F |
| European Union | ≤5°C (41°F) | Similar range |
| Australia | ≤5°C (41°F) | 5°C – 60°C |
| Canada | ≤4°C (39°F) | Similar to US |
| WHO/HACCP (international) | ≤10°C (50°F) for transport | 10°C – 65°C |

---

### Summary: When to Accept or Reject Food

| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Cold food at 41°F (5°C) or below | **ACCEPT** |
| Hot food at 135°F (57°C) or above | **ACCEPT** |
| Frozen food solid at 0°F (-18°C) or below | **ACCEPT** |
| Food in danger zone for under 2 hours | **USE IMMEDIATELY** |
| Food in danger zone for 2-4 hours | **USE NOW or DISCARD** |
| Food in danger zone for over 4 hours | **REJECT/DISCARD** |
| Food with ice crystals or thawed frozen items | **REJECT** |

3. https://ladle.com/resources/blog/safe-food-temperatures-protect-public-health-and-your-bottom-line/
